scope: Primary-source support for a ground-evaluation architecture; not evidence of our flight implementation or qualification.

localBaselines.used: C3 section 10 and RDR-022/023/028 retained as open; naming rocketstar confirmed.
Core/equipment boundary and limited SIM_ONLY proof retained.
Existing RockstarOS operational code is not flight or life-support code.

sources.title: Core Flight System — official bundle README
sources.locator: Core Flight System — BUNDLE; Build and Run; Other Build configurations
sources.verified_summary: cFS is a reusable flight software framework. The public bundle is a starting point, not a flight distribution; mission-specific verification is required. Development configurations include RTEMS targets.
sources.design_application: Select cFS plus RTEMS for ground evaluation; freeze the exact source, RTEMS, CPU/BSP, compiler, and app versions before testing.
sources.limits: The upstream development tree and RTEMS examples do not demonstrate compatibility or flight readiness for this project.

sources.title: Core Flight Executive Version 6.7, GSC-18128-1
sources.verified_summary: cFE provides Software Bus, time, event, executive, table, and file service APIs, supporting portable application development followed by target-platform verification.
sources.design_application: Allocate common infrastructure to cFE and retain mission-specific state estimation, control, and payload applications as separate responsibilities.
sources.limits: This catalog entry describes version 6.7. It is used to substantiate the architecture, not to freeze our deployed release or prove fault isolation.

sources.title: Operating System Abstraction Layer
sources.locator: README: Core Flight System — Framework — Operating System Abstraction Layer
sources.verified_summary: OSAL provides abstraction APIs as a component of the cFS framework and is normally built and tested with cFS.
sources.design_application: Place supported OS service differences behind OSAL while tracking the exact OS port and configuration.
sources.limits: An abstraction API is not evidence of equal timing, driver behavior, memory protection, or qualification across operating systems.

sources.title: Platform Support Package
sources.locator: README: Core Flight System — Framework — Platform Support Package
sources.verified_summary: PSP provides APIs abstracting platform-specific functionality as a cFS framework component.
sources.design_application: Track platform-dependent startup and support separately from mission apps and the RTEMS BSP.
sources.limits: A PSP repository does not supply or qualify every driver, board, and environment required by this mission.

sources.title: RTEMS Classic API Guide 6.1 — Rate Monotonic Manager: Background
sources.verified_summary: RTEMS provides periodic-task statistics, including CPU time, wall time, and missed periods. The application must analyze these observations against its requirements and scheduling assumptions.
sources.design_application: Record task periods, deadlines, worst-case execution bounds, interference, blocking, jitter, and measured misses. Treat utilization and measured maxima as inputs rather than sufficient proof.
sources.limits: The 6.1 API description does not establish cFS-version compatibility or this mission’s actual task rates and timing guarantees.

sources.title: RTEMS User Manual 6.1 — Board Support Packages
sources.locator: Board Support Packages; build/test BSP links
sources.verified_summary: RTEMS documents board support packages for target architectures and platform-specific build and test requirements.
sources.design_application: Require an explicit CPU, BSP, peripheral, toolchain, and test configuration in the evaluation manifest.
sources.limits: A listed architecture or BSP is not evidence of our exact board compatibility, environmental fitness, or mission qualification.

sources.title: RTEMS Classic API Guide 6.1 — Uniprocessor Schedulers
sources.verified_summary: RTEMS offers uniprocessor scheduler configurations, including priority-based scheduling approaches.
sources.design_application: Start timing analysis with an explicit single-CPU fixed-priority evaluation model; reassess if hardware or scheduling changes.
sources.limits: This choice is an analysis baseline, not a decision about flight processor count or demonstrated deadline compliance.

sources.title: Health and Safety Application
sources.verified_summary: The HS application supports application and event monitoring, hardware-watchdog servicing, optional execution-counter reporting, and CPU-aliveness indication.
sources.design_application: Evaluate HS for software health monitoring while defining separate physical protection, fault detection dependencies, and mode-specific recovery.
sources.limits: Running HS on the same CPU does not by itself create independent protection or prove common-cause fault tolerance.

sources.title: F Prime 4.1.0 — Overview
sources.verified_summary: F Prime is a component-based embedded and flight software framework with defined interfaces, queues, threads, modeling tools, reusable components, and tests.
sources.design_application: Retain F Prime as an alternative for A-LINK or instrument software if integration cost and resource evidence favor it.
sources.limits: Framework history and supplied components do not qualify a new deployment or remove OS, CPU, driver, and mission verification work.

sources.title: NASA-STD-8739.8B — Software Assurance and Software Safety Standard
sources.verified_summary: Software hazard analysis considers common-mode failures in redundant computers and preservation of the independence of hazard inhibits and hardware redundancy.
sources.design_application: Separate independent protection from Core, AI, external links, and their shared failure causes; analyze recovery-induced hazards.
sources.limits: Applying this architectural principle does not assert NASA compliance, independent certification, or human-rating.

sources.title: SWE-134 — Safety-Critical Software Design Requirements, Version D
sources.verified_summary: The guidance addresses known-state initialization and transitions, command order, input/output integrity, prerequisites, error handling, and timely response to abnormal conditions.
sources.design_application: Specify equipment-local command checks, mode-dependent behavior, restart conditions, and physically justified response deadlines.
sources.limits: No safety setpoints, hazard deadlines, or compliance status for this project are derived merely by citing the handbook.
